Every year it showed up in the mailbox right around the first frost, thick as a phone book and smelling like fresh ink. Mom would set it on the coffee table and that was the end of homework for a week. My sister and I lay on the living room rug and went through it page by page, pencil in hand. She circled dolls. I circled anything with wheels. By the time Thanksgiving came around, the corners were soft and the spine was cracked from being opened so many times. We never got half of what we circled, and somehow it was still the best part of the whole season.
column6:
My brother wrote his initials next to every circle so nobody could claim his picks. Mom kept that catalog in the hall closet until spring, and I never once asked why.
